problem_statement: The bounded string-formatting routine in dbg-io is unsafe when called with a destination capacity of zero. A user calling it with a buffer of size 0 (for example to query the formatted length without storing output) finds that the supplied destination buffer is modified instead of left untouched: the routine still attempts to write a terminating NUL into the empty region, overwriting whatever was already there, and its remaining-length counter can wrap to a huge value so that a much larger-than-declared region is written, corrupting adjacent memory. Even with a capacity of 1, the behavior is wrong: the routine should place only a terminator and write nothing else. Observable symptom: passing a buffer filled with a known sentinel pattern and requesting size 0 returns the would-be formatted length but the buffer's first byte has been changed from its sentinel value (a buffer overrun), and a size-1 call can also corrupt the buffer. The routine must not write to the destination when there is no room, and must produce a correctly terminated result when capacity is at least 1.
causal_chain: The new native unit tests under tests/08-native-runs/21-dbg-io drive the dbg-io formatting engine directly. test_snprintf_size_zero pre-fills a 16-byte buffer with 0xAA, calls the bounded formatter with size 0 and the format producing "12345", then asserts the return value is 5 and that buf[0] is still 0xAA. At the base, the buffer write callback clamps the copied length as 'len = buffer->left; len--' with buffer->left equal to 0, so the unsigned counter wraps to a very large value and memcpy copies far past the buffer; the formatter then unconditionally writes the terminating NUL into buffer->pos regardless of capacity. Both corrupt buf[0], so the assertion that buf[0] remains 0xAA fails (and the routine overruns the buffer). The production fix makes the write callback return early when there is no capacity left and guards the terminator write on a non-zero size, so a size-0 call writes nothing and leaves the sentinel intact, while the returned would-be length is preserved; this flips the case from fail to pass.
